title: A Kubernetes-supervised replica is probed at /live and /ready on the request-traffic listener with no operator configuration
asA: kubelet running a probing loop against a pod that applied the blueprint with no explicit configuration
iWant: the pod to answer HTTP GET probes at /live and /ready on the container's request-traffic port immediately after boot
soThat: the standard Kubernetes livenessProbe and readinessProbe of shape httpGet: { path: /live, port: <containerPort> } and httpGet: { path: /ready, port: <containerPort> } work without further wiring

acceptanceCriteria.description: A running process on the shipped Kubernetes default answers GET /live with status 200 whenever the event loop is responsive.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a process booted on the shipped `kubernetes` profile default with no operator override, running normally with its event loop responsive
acceptanceCriteria.when: an unauthenticated GET is issued against `/live` on the request-traffic listener port
acceptanceCriteria.then: the response status code is 200 and the JSON body equals `{"status":"pass"}`

acceptanceCriteria.description: The liveness handler on the shipped Kubernetes default performs zero downstream network calls per probe hit.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a network-egress observer attached to the liveness handler on a process running the shipped `kubernetes` default
acceptanceCriteria.then: the observer records zero egress connections attributable to the handler between request receipt and response send

acceptanceCriteria.description: A running process on the shipped Kubernetes default answers GET /ready with 200 when the operator-declared readiness predicate is pass and 503 when it is fail.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a process booted on the shipped `kubernetes` profile default with a readiness predicate wired against a stubbed dependency state
acceptanceCriteria.when: the stubbed state is set to pass and a GET is issued against `/ready`, then the stubbed state is set to fail and a GET is issued again
acceptanceCriteria.then: the first response has status 200 and body `{"status":"pass"}`; the second response has status 503 and body `{"status":"fail"}`

acceptanceCriteria.description: When the operator sets probeInterface.options.kubernetes.startup.enabled: true on the shipped Kubernetes profile, the resolver returns a three-path set including the startup path (default /startup) and the handler-set builder generates a startup handler that answers pass once the operator-declared startup predicate returns pass and fail otherwise.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a process on the shipped kubernetes profile with probeInterface.options.kubernetes.startup.enabled set to true, a startup predicate wired against a stubbed initialisation state, and the paths option left at its default
acceptanceCriteria.when: the resolver runs at boot, and then GETs are issued against /startup with the stubbed state first fail then pass
acceptanceCriteria.then: the resolver returns { profile: kubernetes, paths: [/live, /ready, /startup] }; the first GET on /startup returns 503 with body {"status":"fail"}; the second GET on /startup returns 200 with body {"status":"pass"}; without the enable flag the resolver returns two paths and no /startup handler is registered
